    Extending a hook tackle to a cohook tackle #

    Package the dependent-index construction used in BGRS Lemma 8.4. A compatible replacement for the final hook, together with an incomparable irreducible morphism into the same new peak, extends the old hook tackle by one final cohook.

    IsIrreducibleRayMorphism (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp e f)

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.rayTargetIncomparable_of_not_exists_factor_of_one_lt_depth {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms C] [IsFiniteRayCategory C] [HasFiniteRayPathDepth C] {X Y Z : C} (f : NonzeroHom X Z) (g : NonzeroHom Y Z) (hfdepth : 1 < f.depth) (hg : IsIrreducibleRayMorphism ↑g) (hfactor : ¬∃ (h : X ⟶ Y), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp h ↑g = ↑f) :
    RayTargetIncomparable f g

    For a depth-greater-than-one left ray and an irreducible right ray with the same target, only the factorization of the left ray through the right one must be excluded to obtain target incomparability.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.alternateLists_concat_left_of_length_eq {α : Type u_1} (xs ys : List α) (x : α) (h : xs.length = ys.length) :
    alternateLists (xs.concat x) ys = (alternateLists xs ys).concat x

    Alternating two equally long lists after appending one final entry to the left list appends that entry to the alternating word.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.alternateLists_concat_both_of_length_eq {α : Type u_1} (xs ys : List α) (x y : α) (h : xs.length = ys.length) :
    alternateLists (xs.concat x) (ys.concat y) = alternateLists xs ys ++ [x, y]

    Alternating two equally long lists after appending one entry to each appends those two entries, in left-right order, to the alternating word.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.alternateLists_concat_right_of_length_eq_succ {α : Type u_1} (xs ys : List α) (y : α) (h : xs.length = ys.length + 1) :
    alternateLists xs (ys.concat y) = alternateLists xs ys ++ [y]

    If the left list has one extra entry, appending to the right list appends that entry after the existing alternating word.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.alternateLists_concat_both_of_length_eq_succ {α : Type u_1} (xs ys : List α) (x y : α) (h : xs.length = ys.length + 1) :
    alternateLists (xs.concat x) (ys.concat y) = alternateLists xs ys ++ [y, x]

    If the left list has one extra entry, appending to both lists adds the new right entry and then the new left entry to the alternating word.

      The first propagation step in BGRS Figure 55. If an extension of the last hook is not compatible with the preceding sigma, then it factors through that sigma. The opposite factorization direction would force the old last hook to factor through sigma, contradicting the old tackle valley.
